notes: POOL: 11,799 Commander-legal non-land cards with colour identity subset of B/G (12,331 including lands; lands are excluded because build_plan.json already fixes a 36-land manabase deterministically). Un-set codes unf/sunf/ust/ugl/unh/und/ulst are dropped; the builder's Unfinity sticker-row fix is upstream of me, but cards.csv still marks acorn cards legal_commander=legal, so I drop those set codes by hand. Bracket 4 lifts the mass-land-denial exclusion: only 2 of config.MASS_LAND_DENIAL's 26 names are in identity (Death Cloud, Winter Moon) and neither is archetype-relevant, so the bracket change moved the pool by 3 cards, not by hundreds. The real bracket-4 delta is combos and Game Changers, not pool size.

BRACKET-LIFTED CARDS, now surfaced (flagged bracket_lifted:true, top of flex): Blowfly Infestation (roles removal:debuff; 3 in-identity two-card infinites incl. the one with the commander, popularity 22,904), Host of the Hereafter (roles threat:body only; the second commander two-card infinite, popularity 375), Ivy Lane Denizen (roles buff:counters/threat:body; 14 in-identity two-card infinites, the single densest combo node in the pool), High Perfect Morcant (roles removal:debuff/threat:body; exactly 1 combo in the whole DB). Three of the four carry NO role that would have surfaced them from the taxonomy - combo_details and oracle text did the work.

RULES HAZARD, and it downgrades High Perfect Morcant for THIS commander: Hapatra reads 'Whenever YOU put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature'. Morcant reads 'each opponent blights 1 (They each put a -1/-1 counter on a creature they control)' - the opponent puts the counter, so Morcant does not trigger Hapatra, and does not trigger Nest of Scarabs ('Whenever you put...') either. It DOES trigger Flourishing Defenses ('Whenever a -1/-1 counter IS put on a creature' - passive, any controller). combo_details corroborates: High Perfect Morcant has exactly one entry in the entire 83,250-combo DB, and it is Flourishing Defenses. Self-blight cards ('you blight N' = 'put a -1/-1 counter on a creature you control': Boggart Mischief, Blighted Blackthorn, Sinister Gnarlbark, Gutsplitter Gang, Dream Seizer, Dose of Dawnglow, Bogslither's Embrace, Requiting Hex) DO satisfy Hapatra's 'you put'. The previous pool's blanket claim that blight is a Hapatra trigger is right for self-blight and wrong for opponent-blight. Needs a stack scenario to be asserted as fact.

TWO-CARD INFINITES vs BRACKET TAGS - use the repo's own test, not the tag. 31 of the 41 combo_lines entries have piece_count 2 AND an 'Infinite ...' entry in `produces` (is_infinite_by_produces:true). Spellbook's bracketTag maps E->1..R->4 (config.COMBO_BRACKET_TAGS) and it disagrees with that test in both directions: 'Blowfly Infestation + Hapatra' is a genuine two-card infinite tagged bracket 1, while 'High Perfect Morcant + Flourishing Defenses' is tagged bracket 4 and is_infinite_by_produces is FALSE (its produces are all 'Near-infinite ...', bounded by opponents' creature counts). Same for all four Tombstone Stairwell pairs and for Devoted Druid + Quillspike ('Infinitely large creature until end of turn' is not an 'Infinite ...' produce). Count pieces and read `produces`; the tag is not a power measure.

COMBO CLUSTERS in this pool, by node: Mikaeus, the Unhallowed (16 in-identity two-card infinites - every sac outlet is a kill with a persist body), Ivy Lane Denizen (14), Ashnod's Altar (14), Blasting Station (13), Phyrexian Altar (13), Thran Vigil (12 - the enabler nobody plays), Altar of Dementia (10), Devoted Druid (8), Viscera Seer (8), Carrion Feeder (8), Blowfly Infestation (3). Only 9 of Hapatra's 55 Spellbook combos are fully inside B/G; the other 46 need a colour she does not have (Volrath the Shapestealer, Cathars' Crusade, and a family of clone effects on Grim Poppet).

ROLE-FIX VERIFICATION (all four claimed fixes confirmed against data/card_roles.json, rebuilt 2026-07-25): removal:edict no longer fires on your own sacrifice costs - Viscera Seer ['sac-cost','sac-outlet','threat:body'], Ashnod's Altar ['ramp:rock','sac-cost','sac-outlet'], Carrion Feeder ['buff:counters','sac-cost','sac-outlet','threat:body']. buff:pump now catches modern typal templating (Elvish Archdruid 'Other Elf creatures you control get +1/+1' -> buff:pump). payoff:typal exists and fires (Cover of Darkness). payoff:counters now carries Nest of Scarabs and Flourishing Defenses, which had NO entry at all last pass. The removal bucket is materially more trustworthy than the previous pool's.

NEW BUG - removal:edict residual false positive. config.py:~275 ROLE_PATTERNS['removal:edict'] = r"(?:each|target) (?:opponent|player)[\w\s,']{0,40}? sacrifices?" has no trailing word boundary, so 'sacrifice' matches inside 'sacrificed'. Altar of Dementia ('Sacrifice a creature: Target player mills cards equal to the sacrificed creature's power') is tagged removal:edict and therefore appears in the removal bucket; it is a sac outlet + mill, not removal. Adding \b after sacrifices? would fix it. It is the only false positive I found in the 275-card edict list; the other 4 edict/sac-outlet overlaps (Tergrid, Rakdos Riteknife, Jarad, Catapult Fodder) are genuine.

NEW BUG - wincon:drain misses the canonical aristocrat templating. config.py:273 wincon:drain = r"each opponent loses (?:\d+|x) life|each opponent (?:loses|sacrifices)". Blood Artist and Falkenrath Noble read 'target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life' and are classified threat:body only - no drain role - while Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance ('each opponent loses') classify correctly. For an aristocrats deck this is the single most consequential gap in the taxonomy; I force-included Blood Artist and Falkenrath Noble into wincon with role_source 'text-derived'.

NEW BUG - recursion requires a graveyard phrase. config.py recursion = r"return ... from (?:your|a) graveyard to (?:the battlefield|your hand)". Necroskitter ('Whenever a creature an opponent controls with a -1/-1 counter on it dies, you may return that card to the battlefield under your control') carries threat:body only. Necroskitter is arguably the most on-theme card in the archetype after Hapatra herself and the role index does not see it; force-included into flex, role_source 'text-derived'.

COVERAGE GAP, not a bug - token generation has no role in the taxonomy. Bitterblossom, Parallel Lives and Doubling Season have NO card_roles entry (Doubling Season and Parallel Lives appear in Hapatra's own 4-card Spellbook lines). Also unclassified: Ad Nauseam (Game Changer), Biorhythm (Game Changer, an alt-wincon), Demonic Consultation. Demonic Consultation is an improvement, not a regression: last pass it was mis-tagged removal:sweeper; tutor:unrestricted keys on 'search your library for a card' and Consultation exiles instead, so it now falls through cleanly rather than poisoning the sweeper bucket.

GAME CHANGERS: 29 in B/G identity, 6 of them lands (Ancient Tomb, Gaea's Cradle, Field of the Dead, Glacial Chasm, Mishra's Workshop, The Tabernacle at Pendrell Vale) which the fixed manabase excludes from my remit - flag them to the architect if the land plan is reopened. All 23 non-land Game Changers are surfaced and flagged game_changer:true: Demonic Tutor, The One Ring, Vampiric Tutor, Chrome Mox, Mana Vault, Worldly Tutor, Crop Rotation, Mox Diamond, Orcish Bowmasters, Bolas's Citadel, Seedborn Muse, Necropotence, Imperial Seal, Opposition Agent, Grim Monolith, Lion's Eye Diamond, Ad Nauseam, Tergrid, Natural Order, Survival of the Fittest, Braids Cabal Minion, Panoptic Mirror, Biorhythm. 13 of them reached a bucket only because I force-included them (role_source 'game-changer') - Necropotence is classified 'stax' with no draw role, Seedborn Muse and Opposition Agent are 'threat:body' only. At bracket 4 nothing here is trimmed for count; the architect chooses on merit, not on budget.

theme_score is MY construct, not a repo artifact: a reproducible weighted sum of oracle-text regex flags over cards.csv (payoff-off-counters 3.4, proliferate 2.4, self-blight 2.0, persist 1.8, places -1/-1 counters 1.6 + 1.8 bonus when the controller is you, wither 1.6, sac outlet 1.5, drain 1.6, dies-trigger 1.4, token doubler 1.2, moves counters 1.0, undying 1.0, infect 0.7, toxic 0.3, deathtouch 0.2). Infect is deliberately weighted down from the previous pool: infect creatures do put -1/-1 counters on blocked creatures and so do trigger Hapatra, but vanilla infect bodies were flooding the wincon bucket at no real cost to the -1/-1 plan. Not validated against play results.

similarity is ability-embedding cosine to Hapatra and is REPORTED but NOT trusted for this commander: Nest of Scarabs scores -0.471 and Flourishing Defenses -0.491 - two of the three best cards in the archetype - because the ability embeddings encode function+type, not '-1/-1 payoff'. Ranking is 40/24/14/9/8/5 theme / EDHREC / combo density / commander-combo membership / two-card-infinite membership / synergy-label count for the archetype buckets (removal, sweeper, wincon, flex) and 18/52/12/8/6/4 for the staple buckets (ramp, draw, protection, recursion, tutor). Reproducible; the weights are mine.

SYNERGY GRAPH gave almost nothing here. It is a top-10 retrieval shortlist, and zero cards in the pool list Hapatra in their own top-10, so the only labels available are the 10 on Hapatra's own node ('-1/-1 + Death Trigger', 'Tokens + Sacrifice', 'Counters + Tokens'), of which 6 are in B/G and all skew to 2024-2026 sets (High-Society Hunter, Jerren, The Underworld Fantasy Queen, Sephiroth, Moonstone Eulogist, Jason Bright). Nearly every entry in this pool has no `synergies` key at all; read that as 'the shortlist did not reach here', not 'no synergy'.

WEAKEST BUCKET - SWEEPER (24). Genuine -1/-1-counter sweepers in B/G are Contagion Engine, Black Sun's Zenith, Midnight Banshee, Carnifex Demon, Archfiend of Ifnir, Soul Snuffers, Lockjaw Snapper, Darkness Descends, Harbinger of Night, Liliana's Influence. Everything below those is a generic wrath that also eats your snake tokens; Tombstone Stairwell is in the bucket as a combo piece, not as a sweeper you want to resolve. Black Sun's Zenith was force-included (text-derived) because rank alone put it 5th.

WEAK BUCKET - PROTECTION (24). Still almost entirely generic equipment/hexproof; the only deck-specific piece is Hapatra's Mark (force-included, roles protection:granted/protection:self), which removes -1/-1 counters from your own creature. RECURSION (24) is generic Golgari graveyard value - Persist (the card) was force-included; Necroskitter, the one recursion effect that actually keys off -1/-1 counters, is not in this bucket because the classifier does not see it (see the recursion bug note).

TUTOR (28): materially better than last pass because Game Changers are now permitted - Demonic Tutor #60, Vampiric Tutor #111, Worldly Tutor #166, Imperial Seal #516, Survival of the Fittest #2383, Natural Order #1591 are all surfaced alongside Diabolic Intent, Entomb, Beseech the Mirror, Wishclaw Talisman, Grim Tutor, Green Sun's Zenith, Chord of Calling, Eldritch Evolution and Birthing Pod. card_roles still collapses land-fetch into tutor:narrow, so I filtered ramp:land out of the bucket (which is why Crop Rotation had to be force-added as a Game Changer rather than ranking in).

BUCKET SIZES: ramp 28, draw 28, removal 32, sweeper 24, protection 24, recursion 24, tutor 28, wincon 30, flex 45 = 263 entries over 229 unique cards (30 cards appear in more than one bucket by design, e.g. Yawgmoth in removal/flex, Obelisk Spider in removal/wincon/flex). FLEX is intentionally the largest bucket: this archetype's engine - -1/-1 payoffs, persist bodies, sac outlets, token doublers, aristocrat drains, counter-movers - mostly falls outside the role taxonomy entirely.

EVERY combo_lines entry is status 'needs a stack scenario'. 7 of the 41 name Hapatra explicitly and are `uses_commander:true`; those are the ones most likely to be assuming she is on the battlefield as your commander. Judge's Desk A-004 is the precedent where a Spellbook line survived the graph and was refuted by an actual resolve-stack run. Nothing here has been resolved.

WHAT THE DATA CANNOT SAY: whether any of this is good, what it costs, what the pod looks like, whether Mikaeus's undying and Hapatra's own -1/-1 counters net out favourably on the same board (they interact - undying checks for a +1/+1 counter and Hapatra's counters are -1/-1, and how the two behave on one body is a rules question I have not resolved), and whether 31 two-card infinites is a deck or a pile. Those are resolve-stack, goldfish and coaching questions.

UPGRADES are the raw obsolescence_index and it is noisy for combo pieces: it proposes Basalt Monolith -> Moss Diamond ('Lower CMC', similarity 0.998), which drops the {3}: untap ability that is the only reason the card is in this pool at all. The index compares supertype/tags/CMC/stats, not function-in-a-combo. Treat every row as a question, not an instruction; I truncated to 15 rows.
